Definition: from ὄπις (regard; from G3700) with enclitic of source; from the rear (as a secure aspect), i.e. at the back (adverb and preposition of place or time):--after, backside, behind.
BiblicalUsage: Behind is where the desperate find Jesus. The woman with the issue of blood came behind Him in the crowd and touched the border of His garment, and Mark tells the same story of a woman who pressed through the press behind Him.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the woman who came behind Jesus teaches me something plain: faith does not need a face-to-face appointment, only a touch.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
